seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering horizontal projection from towers, trajectory parabola equation, radius of curvature, hunter-monkey theorem, and staircase stepping problems.

conceptCapsule.title: Kinematics of Horizontally Projected Bodies
conceptCapsule.summary: When a projectile is launched horizontally from height $h$ with initial velocity $u$: (1) Horizontal motion is uniform: $u_x = u$, $a_x = 0$, $x(t) = ut$. (2) Vertical motion is free fall from rest: $u_y = 0$, $a_y = g$, $y(t) = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$. (3) Time of flight depends exclusively on height: $T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$. (4) Horizontal range: $R = uT = u\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$. (5) Parabolic trajectory: $y = -\frac{g}{2u^2}x^2$. (6) Striking speed: $v = \sqrt{u^2 + 2gh}$.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: The time of flight for a horizontal projectile is entirely independent of its launch speed $u$. Two bodies projected horizontally from the same height with different horizontal velocities will hit the ground simultaneously ($T_1 = T_2$). At the moment of release, the radius of curvature is $R = \frac{u^2}{g}$ because $a_n = g$ acts perpendicular to $\vec{v}_0$.

questions.statement: A projectile is launched horizontally from a height $h$ with an initial velocity $u$. The time of flight $T$ depends on:
questions.solution:
Vertical motion is free fall under gravity with zero initial vertical velocity ($u_y = 0$): $$h = \frac{1}{2}g T^2 \implies T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$$ The time of flight $T$ is completely independent of the horizontal launch velocity $u$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: An aeroplane flying horizontally at a height of $490\text{ m}$ with a speed of $180\text{ km/h}$ drops a food packet. The horizontal distance covered by the packet before hitting the ground is: (Take $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Speed $u = 180 \times \frac{5}{18} = 50\text{ m/s}$.
2. Time of flight: $T = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2(490)}{9.8}} = 10\text{ s}$.
3. Horizontal range: $R = u \times T = 50 \times 10 = 500\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected horizontally from the top of a cliff of height $H$ with speed $u$. The equation of its trajectory taking the launch point as the origin is:
questions.solution:
1. $x = ut \implies t = \frac{x}{u}$
2. $y = -\frac{1}{2}gt^2 = -\frac{1}{2}g\left(\frac{x}{u}\right)^2 = -\frac{g}{2u^2}x^2$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A ball is projected horizontally from a tower with speed $u = 20\text{ m/s}$. The angle made by the velocity vector with the horizontal after $2\text{ seconds}$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. $v_x = u = 20\text{ m/s}$
2. $v_y = gt = 10(2) = 20\text{ m/s}$
3. $\tan\theta = \frac{v_y}{v_x} = \frac{20}{20} = 1 \implies \theta = 45^\circ$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two bodies $A$ and $B$ are projected horizontally from the top of a tower with velocities $u_1$ and $u_2$ ($u_1 > u_2$) respectively. If $T_1$ and $T_2$ are their respective times of flight, then:
questions.solution:
Since both bodies are projected from the same vertical height $h$ with zero initial vertical velocity, their vertical kinematics are identical: $$T_1 = T_2 = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A stone is projected horizontally with velocity $u$ from the top of a tower. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at the point of projection is:
questions.solution:
At the moment of horizontal projection: speed is $v = u$, and acceleration perpendicular to velocity is $a_n = g$. Radius of curvature: $$R = \frac{v^2}{a_n} = \frac{u^2}{g}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A ball is thrown horizontally from the top of a tower of height $80\text{ m}$ with speed $u = 30\text{ m/s}$. The speed with which it strikes the ground is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. $v_x = u = 30\text{ m/s}$
2. $v_y = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(10)(80)} = 40\text{ m/s}$
3. Striking speed $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = 50\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A hunter aims his rifle horizontally directly at a monkey sitting on a tree branch at height $h$. The monkey drops from the branch at the exact instant the bullet leaves the muzzle. The bullet will:

options.text: Always hit the monkey regardless of the muzzle speed $u$ (provided $u$ is large enough to bridge the distance)

questions.solution:
In time $t$, the bullet drops vertically by $y_b = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ from the sight line, while the monkey drops by $y_m = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ from the branch. Both undergo identical vertical displacements at any given instant, guaranteeing that the bullet hits the monkey.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A ball is thrown horizontally from the top of an inclined plane of inclination $\theta$ with speed $u$. The time of flight of the ball before hitting the incline is:
questions.solution:
1. Horizontal coordinate: $x = ut$, Vertical drop: $y = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
2. On the incline surface: $\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}gt^2}{ut} = \frac{gt}{2u} \implies t = \frac{2u\tan\theta}{g}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Q9, the distance along the incline from the launch point to where the ball lands is:
questions.solution:
1. $x = ut = u\left(\frac{2u\tan\theta}{g}\right) = \frac{2u^2\tan\theta}{g}$
2. Slant distance along incline: $$L = \frac{x}{\cos\theta} = \frac{2u^2\tan\theta\sec\theta}{g}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A projectile fired horizontally from a height $h$ lands at a horizontal distance equal to $2h$. The launch speed $u$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $R = u \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = 2h$
2. Squaring: $u^2\left(\frac{2h}{g}\right) = 4h^2 \implies u^2 = 2gh \implies u = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected horizontally from a height with speed $u$. The instant at which the tangential acceleration equals the centripetal (normal) acceleration is:
questions.solution:
1. Tangential acceleration: $a_t = g\sin\theta$, Normal acceleration: $a_n = g\cos\theta$.
2. $a_t = a_n \implies \tan\theta = 1 \implies \theta = 45^\circ$.
3. $\tan\theta = \frac{v_y}{v_x} = \frac{gt}{u} = 1 \implies t = \frac{u}{g}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Two stones are projected horizontally in opposite directions from the top of a tower with velocities $u_1$ and $u_2$. The time after which their velocity vectors become mutually perpendicular is:
questions.solution:
1. $\vec{v}_1 = u_1\hat{i} - gt\hat{j}$, $\vec{v}_2 = -u_2\hat{i} - gt\hat{j}$
2. $\vec{v}_1 \cdot \vec{v}_2 = 0 \implies -u_1 u_2 + g^2 t^2 = 0 \implies t = \frac{\sqrt{u_1 u_2}}{g}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Q13, the separation between the two stones at the instant their velocity vectors are mutually perpendicular is:
questions.solution:
Separation $x_{\text{rel}} = (u_1 + u_2)t = \frac{(u_1 + u_2)\sqrt{u_1 u_2}}{g}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A ball rolls off the top of a staircase with horizontal velocity $u$. If the steps are of uniform height $h$ and width $b$, the ball will hit the $n\text{th}$ step if $n$ satisfies:
questions.solution:
1. Coordinates of edge of $n^{\text{th}}$ step: $x = nb$, $y = nh$.
2. $nh = \frac{1}{2}g\left(\frac{nb}{u}\right)^2 = \frac{gn^2 b^2}{2u^2} \implies n = \frac{2u^2 h}{gb^2}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A bomber flies horizontally at speed $u$ at height $H$. A target is stationary on the ground. The angle $\phi$ with the horizontal at which the target must be seen by the sight-line at the moment of bomb release is:
questions.solution:
1. Horizontal range: $R = u \sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$.
2. Sight line angle with horizontal: $$\tan\phi = \frac{H}{R} = \frac{H}{u\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}} = \frac{\sqrt{gH}}{\sqrt{2}u} \implies \phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{gH}}{\sqrt{2}u}\right)$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected horizontally from a height $h$. The displacement of the particle when its velocity vector makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the horizontal has magnitude:
questions.solution:
1. At $45^\circ$: $v_y = v_x = u \implies gt = u \implies t = u/g$.
2. $x = ut = u^2/g$, $y = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = \frac{u^2}{2g}$.
3. Magnitude $r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{(u^2/g)^2 + (u^2/2g)^2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}u^2}{2g}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: From the top of a tower of height $H$, a particle is projected horizontally with speed $u$. The rate at which the distance $r$ from the projection point increases initially ($t \to 0$) is:
questions.solution:
Distance $r(t) = \sqrt{u^2 t^2 + \frac{1}{4}g^2 t^4} = ut\sqrt{1 + \frac{g^2 t^2}{4u^2}}$. Taking the derivative $\frac{dr}{dt}$ at $t \to 0$ gives $u$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A stone is projected horizontally with velocity $u = 10\text{ m/s}$ from a tower. At time $t = 1\text{ s}$, the radius of curvature of the trajectory is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. At $t = 1\text{ s}$: $v_x = 10\text{ m/s}$, $v_y = 10\text{ m/s} \implies v = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$, $\theta = 45^\circ$.
2. Normal acceleration: $a_n = g\cos(45^\circ) = \frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ m/s}^2$.
3. Radius of curvature: $$R = \frac{v^2}{a_n} = \frac{(10\sqrt{2})^2}{10/\sqrt{2}} = \frac{200}{10/\sqrt{2}} = 20\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle is projected horizontally from the top of a tower. During its motion, the horizontal component of acceleration $a_x$ and vertical component $a_y$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
Neglecting air resistance, no horizontal force acts on the projectile ($a_x = 0$), while gravity acts purely vertically downward ($a_y = g$).
Therefore, Option A is correct.
